title: Count balls: what is settled by construction and by classical results
claim: S1: on split bases the disagreement count is twice the number of separating splits; on boxes twice the L1 distance (ball the cross-polytope, Golab pi 4 in two orders, k = lam = d); on every base with lam = 2 twice the L1 distance of its two orders (NN's grids). S2: the 2 x m ladder (k = lam = 2) and the comb (k = 1) have outlines of 4 at every count from a middle start, so one start's growth does not read k (every start's growth together tells these two apart; narrowed after referee R1). S3: parity bases are blank. S4: on the state side every parity state sees the weight enumerator; the state metric is blind to translation by a state; rooted at the all-equal state it determines k and lam. S5: a chain of l not-all-equal knots with loose distinctions is the pair law (w_eq - w_ne)/(w_eq + w_ne) = (-1/3)^l (high-temperature Ising), with the gauge sign and the loose identity. S6 (cited): the chain grid's count outline is the polar of {cosh q1 + cosh q2 <= A}, strictly convex and analytic for every l, tending to the taxicab diamond (Golab pi -> 4). S7 (cited): on the weave C ~ a r^(-1/2) cos(Q.r), a = 0.6322260823, isotropic.
standard_statement: Split metrics and lattice dimension; Ising correlation-length shape above Tc; zero-temperature triangular antiferromagnet correlations; Hamming geometry of codes.
